title: Quantum Transformer BSDE Solver via Multi-Layer Fully-Connected Variational Quantum Circuits
authors: Howard Su, Huan-Hsin Tseng, Chi-Sheng Chen, Lance Bai
abstract: Solving high-dimensional parabolic partial differential equations (PDEs) is important in engineering, physics, and stochastic control. Deep BSDE methods reformulate semilinear PDEs as backward stochastic differential equations and admit a model-based reinforcement learning interpretation, where trajectories are generated from known stochastic dynamics while a trainable model learns the gradient-related control process. We propose a Quantum Transformer BSDE solver based on Multi-Layer Fully-Connected Variational Quantum Circuits (FC-VQC). The method treats the normalized state trajectory as time--coordinate tokens and applies causal self-attention to learn interactions in the adapted BSDE gradient process. All trainable model parameters are contained within the FC-VQC embedding, projection, feed-forward, and decoder modules, while attention and structural operations remain classical and parameter-free. Experiments on three d=36 PDE benchmarks show that QTransformer consistently improves over the non-attentive FC-VQC baseline and outperforms the classical Transformer at compact hidden widths, while the wider classical Transformer achieves the best overall accuracy. These results demonstrate that combining causal attention with FC-VQC provides an effective quantum architecture for high-dimensional BSDE trajectory learning.
summary: This paper introduces a Quantum Transformer solver that uses Multi-Layer Fully-Connected Variational Quantum Circuits (FC-VQC) to solve complex, high-dimensional Partial Differential Equations reformulated as BSDEs. By integrating causal self-attention into the quantum circuit structure, the model achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to classical and non-attentive quantum baselines on several physical benchmarks.
main_problem: The core problem is solving high-dimensional parabolic partial differential equations (PDEs) by reformulating them into Backward Stochastic Differential Equations (BSDEs). This is crucial in fields like stochastic control and physics.
main_result: The proposed Quantum Transformer solver consistently improves upon non-attentive quantum circuit baselines, demonstrating that combining causal attention with FC-VQC provides an effective architecture for high-dimensional BSDE trajectory learning.
method: The authors propose a Quantum Transformer model where trainable parameters are confined within Multi-Layer Fully-Connected Variational Quantum Circuits (FC-VQC) modules integrated into the standard Transformer structure. Causal self-attention is used to process time-coordinate tokens derived from the state trajectory.
model_or_system: The method targets solving BSDEs associated with semilinear PDEs (e.g., Black–Scholes, Burgers-type). The quantum component uses FC-VQC circuits to parameterize the necessary mappings within the Transformer architecture.
key_observables: Mean Trajectory Relative L2 Error (LRE) and Relative Mean Absolute Error (RelMAE), with lower values indicating better performance across three benchmark PDEs.
important_parameters: Model depth ($L \in \{3, 5, 7\}$) and hidden dimension ($d_m$). The comparison highlights the effect of attention versus non-attentive circuits.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that structural operations (like attention mechanisms) can remain classical and parameter-free while confining all trainable parameters to scalable FC-VQC modules.
figures_summary: Table I compares LRE across various model configurations (DNN, FC-VQC, Transformer, QTransformer). Figure 1 illustrates the integrated Quantum Transformer architecture using FC-VQC modules in key layers.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of solving PDEs via BSDEs. It then details the novel QTransformer architecture integrating FC-VQC into the Transformer framework. Results are presented by comparing performance against classical and non-attentive quantum baselines on multiple benchmarks, concluding with an analysis of architectural components.
why_interesting: While the application is numerical PDE solving, the core innovation lies in mapping complex functional approximation tasks onto hybrid quantum-classical neural network architectures (QTransformer/FC-VQC), which has implications for simulating quantum dynamics or high-dimensional physical systems.
